question: Does a crossing binding survive an intermediary that holds its own downstream credential?

cases.description: A legitimate request from the original caller, carried through the broker with an intact crossing binding, targeting the agent the binding names.
cases.prediction: succeed in both. If this fails in either lane the experiment is void, because every later refusal would be consistent with a broken lane rather than a broker-introduced gap.

cases.description: The broker authenticates downstream as itself, using its own registered credential, rather than presenting evidence naming the original caller.
cases.mutation: downstream sees broker identity in place of original requester identity
cases.must: be refused in the brokered lane only if the binding names the original requester and that name is checked downstream

cases.description: A second, separately authenticated caller reaches the same broker route. The broker's downstream credential is unchanged. The first caller's crossing binding is still in the broker's possession.
cases.mutation: requester substituted upstream of the broker while the broker's downstream credential stays constant
cases.must: be refused; caller B must not be able to cause an action bound to caller A's evidence

cases.description: The broker presents a well-formed crossing binding that it was never given by any caller in this exchange.
cases.mutation: binding fabricated at the broker rather than relayed

cases.description: The crossing binding is genuine, unexpired and correctly signed, but names a different downstream agent than the one the broker routes to.
cases.mutation: downstream target substituted while the binding remains internally valid

cases.description: The original caller's authority is revoked. The broker's own downstream credential remains valid and unrevoked.
cases.mutation: upstream authority revoked, intermediary credential still live

notClaimed: That any named product implements the brokered lane in this shape. The broker is modelled from the composition pattern observed in the 2026-08-19 refutation check, not copied from any implementation.
That A2A, MCP, or any gateway is defective. This measures whether a binding degrades across an intermediary, not whether anyone's code is wrong.
That either composition direction is the more common production shape. That is a survey question and is out of scope here.
